This deposit is an archival copy made so that the full text stays retrievable; it makes no separate claim. When an AI model says gold will rise, anyone can score the call at the close, but few can check when it was made. A backtest mixes memory with skill, and an operator's log asks for trust. I propose a standard for measuring AI market forecasts, written as a ladder of checkable requirements, and I run its reference implementation, AI Council · Markets: an open league where fourteen models, seven from US and seven from Chinese laboratories, face one question on one price snapshot. Before each New York open the ten on its Council, five from each side, give probabilities for twelve indicators at four horizons. Each answer is sealed into a hash chain before the price it is scored from, the chain is anchored in Bitcoin and signed by independent time-stamping authorities, and one run per session counts by a rule declared in advance. On 21 October 2026, the first counted morning, every counted answer was signed before the 09:30 ET open. Agreement among the models proved to be a count of independent voices, not a headcount: on two development mornings the seven and eight models sealed before the open were as alike as about 1.6 independent forecasters, nine counted ones were worth 2.23, and the closest pairs crossed the US-China line. Check a seal with three commands, and score my thirty predictions, registered on OSF, before I do.

items.summary: Background/Objectives : With the advent of the current digital health age, opportunities for interacting with health systems have grown not only more frequent but also variable in type, spanning across emergent care settings, routine outpatient follow-up, as well as at-home telemedicine-based platforms. In light of initiatives to re-design electronic medical records (EMR) to more meaningfully curate evidence-based insights, our research objective is focused on harnessing underutilized data features (i.e., time-ordered events) to map the complex interactions that patients undergo within their health systems. We posit that inclusion of information associated with sequential patterns will help more accurately simulate care pathways and outcomes. We report preliminary data on care utilization patterns among cohorts of patients diagnosed with chronic disease. Methods : De-identified data were extracted from the MedStar Health AIM-AHEAD Data Bridge (AADB)’s Chronic Disease repository. EMRs were queried for patients with confirmed diagnoses for diabetes mellitus (ICD-10: E10.X or E11.X) as well as heart failure (ICD-10: I50.X). For each unique patient, encounters related to care utilization were sequentially collated, with explicit demarcation of whether interactions occurred before or after corresponding diagnoses. For analytical purposes, encounters were categorized as “Emergency”, “Inpatient”, “Observation”, “Outpatient”, “Home Health”, and “Patient Portal”. For each cohort, sequential pattern mining (SPM) was used to generate antecedent-consequent prediction rules and calculate the conditional probabilities (confidence) of subsequent care utilization episodes. Analyses were performed using R (The R Foundation for Statistical Computing; version 4.5.2). Results : Between January 2018 and December 2024, we distinctly identified 202,605 patients with a diagnosis for diabetes mellitus as well as 79,223 patients with a diagnosis for heart failure. Across both cohorts, 42,208 patients had documentation of being diagnosed with both conditions and were flagged separately for potential sensitivity analyses. The proportion of older patients (50 years or above) was predominant (>85% for all patients). The median number of annual healthcare interactions tended to increase post-diagnosis (versus pre-diagnosis) particularly in diabetic cohorts: 3.0 versus 1.0 (diabetes only); 5.0 versus 1.7 (diabetes and heart failure). Total instances of care episodes (t) were enumerated across the 7-year study period: diabetes only (t=3,511,417), heart failure only (t=741,789), diabetes and heart failure (t=1,681,307). SPM algorithms were used to generate rulebooks associating unique care utilization patterns with their corresponding likelihood of subsequent events. Discussion/Conclusions : Our initial findings highlight a wide variability of care utilization patterns among patients diagnosed with chronic diseases. We demonstrated that analyzing care utilization sequences may yield embedded insights that can be harnessed for prospectively tracking person-centered health trajectories. The current work exhibits several limitations and opportunities for expanded analysis. We expect to enrich our data pipeline with more detailed clinical features (e.g., medications, laboratory panels, procedures) in future iterations. This comprehensive ingestion would enable the initial steps towards developing models for predicting the onset of unfavorable health outcomes. Implications: Notwithstanding these considerations, the goals of our preliminary efforts are aligned with learning health systems models which emphasize the implementation of evidence-based insights at the point-of-care. items.summary: This paper develops the Phase Compatibility branch of Harmonic Physics: a framework for examining how physical participants enter constrained phase relations, produce collective outcomes, and form persistent higher-level organisations capable of further recursive participation. Building on established synchronization theory, phase locking, coupled-oscillator dynamics and phasor mathematics, the framework examines reinforcement, opposition, cancellation, reshaping and whole formation. It distinguishes mathematical admissibility, actual source occupancy, participant admission, active interaction, closure, continuing identity and observation. A compatibility basin is characterised through maintained relational organisation and persistence under declared conditions. Version 3.1 aligns the shared definitions with the current Foundations and Observer Theory papers, corrects the amplitude-weighted moment family, and clarifies the distinction between passive changes of representation and physical projection or coupling. It incorporates the completed mathematical nesting construction, which preserves a supplied quantum state’s amplitude and relative-phase information, together with Born probabilities under corresponding joint measurements. Phase Theory Equations is identified as the consolidated reference for the current mathematical expressions. The observation account separates source organisation, information encoded into light, receiver coupling, registration, retention and calibrated reconstruction. Within the proposed optical terminology, light performs the observer role through source–receiver coupling, while the receiver registers and retains a physical response. Minimal relational consciousness and awareness retain separate definitions. The paper integrates controlled models, molecular spectral studies, a superconducting-qubit analogue, simulated liquid-water reorganisation, quantum-state encoding and specified receiver models, preserving the scope and limitations of each result. It sets out the state spaces, conservation requirements, comparison models and prospective failure conditions required for physical applications. Universal participant-admission and whole-formation laws remain open research questions; this revision introduces no new experimental validation.

items.summary: RASHER begins as a fork of BACoN 0.4.0 (commit 4fdec16, which includes the samtools consensus -C 20 change below), adapted to Illumina short reads. Everything under "BACoN changelog" is the parent tool's history, kept for provenance. Changed Renamed throughout: the package, command, log ( rasher.log ) and lock file ( .rasher.lock ) are rasher . The pipeline reads Illumina short reads , paired or single-end. sample_R1 / sample_R2 , sample_1 / _2 sample.R1 / .R2 and sample.1 / .2 files (bcl2fastq _001 tails included) pair into one sample, in flat folders, subfolders and sample sheets; a file without a mate is a single-end sample, and unmated files next to a sample's pairs are skipped with a warning. A pair is baited whole when either mate matches the reference, mates travel together through every step ( 1_extracted/<sample>_R1/_R2 , 2_filtered/... ), and a desynchronised pair is an error, whether the mates carry identical names or /1 /2 suffixes. Baiting aligns with minimap2 -x sr (BBDuk baits pairs natively with in2= / outm2= ). --keep-bam now keeps the baited reads aligned to the reference (paired samples: a proper paired BAM). Filtering: fastp (adapter trimming, quality and length filters; its JSON and HTML reports land in logs/2_filter/ where MultiQC finds them) followed by deterministic, evenly spread subsampling of the reads (pairs kept whole) to --target-depth . Filtlong, --keep-percent and --filter-by-reference are gone; --min-read-length defaults to 50. Fasta reads skip fastp and are filtered by length. Templated assembly aligns pairs with minimap2 -ax sr and calls samtools consensus -X hiseq (call quality at least 20, as BACoN's unreleased change at the time of the fork). De novo assembly: SKESA ( -a skesa ; the recommended de novo assembler — on the real-data benchmark its SNP distances matched SPAdes' with far fewer contigs) or SPAdes ( -a spades , --isolate ; writes the assembly graph, more robust below ~30x depth). Flye and myloasm are gone, with --read-type and --min-size . --snp-method auto is minimap2 for templated assemblies and SKA2 for SPAdes and SKESA assemblies. -m/--memory also sizes SPAdes and SKESA (it was BBDuk-only). A paired sample X next to a sample named X_R1 or X_R2 is an error (their outputs would collide). No assembler flags circular contigs any more, so SKA2's circular-contig end extension no longer applies. Single-end extraction matches read names with a trailing /1 or /2 stripped, as aligners report them. Output folders of BACoN do not resume under RASHER (the checkpoint fingerprints are seeded with the tool's name; every step runs again); BACoN VCFs are rewritten. Checkpoints record each step's own output signature, and a result is only reused when its output is still the file it wrote: a sample returning to a sheet can no longer pick up reads another sample wrote over. Switching a sample between single-end and paired (or fasta and fastq) removes the other shape's files. BBDuk's paired outputs are checked mate against mate, like minimap2's (a desynchronised pair fails the sample); mates named .1 / .2 ( fastq-dump --readids ) pair; the unpaired-reads file of fasterq-dump --split-3 next to its pair is skipped with a warning; a file cannot pair with a link to itself, and files that look like mates but do not pair are warned about. Stale fastp reports are removed on rerun and for samples that fail at baiting. The report and MultiQC drop the circular-contigs column (no short-read assembler flags circles) and say that read pairs were kept whole when either mate matched.

items.summary: RFT-FaultBench provides training-process telemetry for anomaly detection and failure-type diagnosis in reinforcement fine-tuning. This revised dataset contains 2,630 runs (339 normal and 2,291 injected), 72,100 train-step records, and 2,617,600 training trajectories across OpenRLHF, AgentEvolver, and TRL and five task categories: arithmetic reasoning, GSM8K-style mathematical reasoning, code generation, verifiable instruction following, and tool calling. It includes 55 compound-failure runs for detection; diagnosis uses 2,236 single-failure runs. Task versions and native failure-label coverage differ across frameworks. The package includes run-level artifacts, canonical labels and seeds, five seed-grouped evaluation folds, 25 one-shot support draws, provenance and exclusion ledgers, per-file checksums, and Python example loaders and validation tools. Membership follows the frozen 2026-10-12 evaluation snapshot. It updates the earlier 779-run release; no new training was performed during packaging. GitHub companion: AIOps4LLM/RFT-FaultBench . Related manuscript: Towards Robust LLM Post-Training: Automatic Failure Diagnosis for Reinforcement Fine-Tuning. Extract RFT-FaultBench-full.tar.gz and consult its README and docs for schemas, verification evidence, and evaluation scope. items.summary: We study intransitive probabilistic preferences through dice whose face labels may be repeated. We distinguish restricted models, in which the set of permitted labels depends on the number of sides, from the unrestricted model, which allows arbitrary integer labels. We review existence results, including the exceptional impossibility of a Chinese chain of five four-sided dice, and give an explicit construction establishing the known existence of simple cycles of three-sided dice of every length m ≥3, with no ties and a net win margin of one. We examine mixed-integer programming, simulated annealing, and lexicographic optimization of the margins. We then extend pairwise comparison to probability measures by means of bounded, measurable, antisymmetric kernels. For complete comparison data with uniform weights, we derive the Hodge decomposition of the margin matrix into an additive score component and an orthogonal, divergence-free residual. We distinguish the failure of an exact additive representation from the existence of strict preference cycles. The minimax theorem ensures that every finite family admits a mixed strategy with nonnegative expected margin against every mixture of that family. For the historical cycle with margins 4, 4, 10, we compute both the decomposition and the equilibrium mixture (2/9, 5/9, 2/9). Applications to portfolios, artistic evaluation, visual perception, and sports clarify the distinctions among independent comparisons, shared scenarios, and expected utility.

items.summary: Highlights of the Study This comprehensive review examines the fatigue behaviour of load-bearing polymeric bone scaffolds , addressing a critical but comparatively underexplored aspect of bone tissue engineering. It evaluates the mechanisms governing fatigue damage and systematically examines how polymer characteristics, microstructure, reinforcing materials, scaffold topology, manufacturing methods, loading conditions, body fluids, and tissue ingrowth influence fatigue performance, with particular emphasis on translating polymeric scaffolds toward reliable load-bearing clinical applications. Key findings: 🟢 Fatigue failure mechanisms: Polymeric scaffolds can undergo both mechanical and thermal fatigue. Repeated cyclic loading causes residual-strain accumulation, stiffness and peak-stress reduction, crack development, and hysteretic heating, which can progressively degrade polymer chains and ultimately cause structural failure. 🟢 Low- and high-cycle fatigue: Low-cycle fatigue generally occurs under relatively high stresses and involves repeated plastic deformation, whereas high-cycle fatigue develops over much larger numbers of cycles under lower stress levels and is primarily associated with elastic deformation and progressive material degradation. 🟢 Material and microstructural effects: Polymer fatigue resistance is strongly governed by molecular and microstructural characteristics. Increased crystallinity, molecular weight, and molecular-chain entanglement can improve fatigue resistance, emphasizing the importance of selecting and tailoring the polymer microstructure for load-bearing scaffolds. 🟢 Reinforcement strategy: Incorporating ceramic or metallic reinforcing phases can substantially improve the fatigue performance of polymeric scaffolds by redistributing applied loads and dissipating energy that would otherwise contribute to polymer deformation and heat generation. 🟢 Hydroxyapatite reinforcement: Incorporation of 15 wt% hydroxyapatite increased the fatigue limit of PLA scaffolds by approximately 17%, while also improving compressive modulus, crack resistance, and hysteresis energy compared with unreinforced PLA. 🟢 Scaffold topology: Pore architecture plays a decisive role in fatigue behaviour by controlling stress distribution and stress concentration. Even scaffolds fabricated from the same polymer and having comparable porosity can exhibit substantially different fatigue lives when their pore geometry and filament arrangement are changed. 🟢 Topology-dependent fatigue life: Among 3D-printed PLA scaffolds with comparable porosity, the tetragonal topology achieved a fatigue life of approximately 4400 cycles, outperforming hexagonal and wheel-like structures at approximately 3200 and 2500 cycles, respectively. 🟢 Advanced scaffold architectures: TPMS, Voronoi, functionally graded, auxetic, and other irregular architectures offer promising approaches for load-bearing scaffolds. TPMS structures are particularly attractive because their smooth transitions at strut junctions may reduce stress concentrations, although their polymer fatigue behaviour remains insufficiently investigated. 🟢 Bone-inspired architecture: Bio-inspired scaffold design can substantially improve fatigue performance. items.summary: Highlights of the Study This comprehensive review examines the fatigue behaviour of load-bearing polymeric bone scaffolds , addressing a critical but comparatively underexplored aspect of bone tissue engineering. It evaluates the mechanisms governing fatigue damage and systematically examines how polymer characteristics, microstructure, reinforcing materials, scaffold topology, manufacturing methods, loading conditions, body fluids, and tissue ingrowth influence fatigue performance, with particular emphasis on translating polymeric scaffolds toward reliable load-bearing clinical applications. Key findings: 🟢 Fatigue failure mechanisms: Polymeric scaffolds can undergo both mechanical and thermal fatigue. Repeated cyclic loading causes residual-strain accumulation, stiffness and peak-stress reduction, crack development, and hysteretic heating, which can progressively degrade polymer chains and ultimately cause structural failure. 🟢 Low- and high-cycle fatigue: Low-cycle fatigue generally occurs under relatively high stresses and involves repeated plastic deformation, whereas high-cycle fatigue develops over much larger numbers of cycles under lower stress levels and is primarily associated with elastic deformation and progressive material degradation. 🟢 Material and microstructural effects: Polymer fatigue resistance is strongly governed by molecular and microstructural characteristics. Increased crystallinity, molecular weight, and molecular-chain entanglement can improve fatigue resistance, emphasizing the importance of selecting and tailoring the polymer microstructure for load-bearing scaffolds. 🟢 Reinforcement strategy: Incorporating ceramic or metallic reinforcing phases can substantially improve the fatigue performance of polymeric scaffolds by redistributing applied loads and dissipating energy that would otherwise contribute to polymer deformation and heat generation. 🟢 Hydroxyapatite reinforcement: Incorporation of 15 wt% hydroxyapatite increased the fatigue limit of PLA scaffolds by approximately 17%, while also improving compressive modulus, crack resistance, and hysteresis energy compared with unreinforced PLA. 🟢 Scaffold topology: Pore architecture plays a decisive role in fatigue behaviour by controlling stress distribution and stress concentration. Even scaffolds fabricated from the same polymer and having comparable porosity can exhibit substantially different fatigue lives when their pore geometry and filament arrangement are changed. 🟢 Topology-dependent fatigue life: Among 3D-printed PLA scaffolds with comparable porosity, the tetragonal topology achieved a fatigue life of approximately 4400 cycles, outperforming hexagonal and wheel-like structures at approximately 3200 and 2500 cycles, respectively. 🟢 Advanced scaffold architectures: TPMS, Voronoi, functionally graded, auxetic, and other irregular architectures offer promising approaches for load-bearing scaffolds. TPMS structures are particularly attractive because their smooth transitions at strut junctions may reduce stress concentrations, although their polymer fatigue behaviour remains insufficiently investigated. 🟢 Bone-inspired architecture: Bio-inspired scaffold design can substantially improve fatigue performance. Increasing the thickness of transverse rod-like struts in bone-inspired structures was reported to enhance fatigue life by approximately 10–100 times with relatively minor effects on density and stiffness. 🟢 Porosity–strength trade-off: Increasing porosity promotes permeability, vascularization, cell migration, and tissue ingrowth but simultaneously reduces scaffold stiffness, strength, and load-bearing capacity. Therefore, successful scaffold design requires balancing biological benefits against fatigue and mechanical integrity. 🟢 Stress concentration: Geometrical discontinuities and sharp pore corners create localized stress concentrations that accelerate fatigue damage. items.summary: Two datasets recording immigration detention oversight in the inspecting bodies' and ICE's own published language. The inspections dataset (207 rows) gives the most recent published inspection per facility from ICE Office of Detention Oversight reports in the ICE FOIA Library 2025–2026 listing window (179 facilities) plus the 28 facility-specific DHS Office of Inspector General detention inspection reports of fiscal years 2021–2026, with each report's published Facility Rating and deficient-standards count reproduced verbatim, never re-graded. The deaths dataset (84 rows) lists the deaths in ICE custody in ICE's Detainee Death Reporting tables for fiscal years 2021–2026, each with the ICE death report ICE itself published (name, age, country of citizenship, facility, date of death, and cause of death where the report states one). Sources: ICE FOIA Library, DHS Office of Inspector General, and ICE Detainee Death Reporting, retrieved October 23, 2026. Tool: https://inspections-ledger.straitresearch.org/. Direction and final calls by Athena Anthea; research judgment and technical execution shared with an AI assistant. Version 1.1 (October 24, 2026) adds: a published facility-name crosswalk (200 canonical facilities) with single-facility dossiers joining ODO, OIG, and deaths records per facility; an extraction naming the deficient standards behind the published counts for 52 of the 179 ODO inspection rows (validated by hand-checking 10 reports; coverage and per-row failure reasons stated, never guessed); and deaths tables showing cause stated (12) vs not stated (72) by fiscal year and facility.
items.title: Inspections & Deaths Ledger: detention facility inspection results and deaths in ICE custody from the official record — a Strait Research dataset

items.summary: The work builds a foundation of physics from a single assumption: everything is a process, and a process is an ideal sine; its centre, the balance, is the observer. Only the square — intensity without phase — passes between levels; from this arise dimensions, the arrow of time, the quantum and the standard. On this basis stable particles are built as standing waves together with their galactic analogues, the initial rules of quantum mechanics and relativity are derived, and the constants are linked to a single number — the speed of light. Agreement with experiment is at the level of a few percent; the model attributes the discrepancies to the imperfection of the standard. Main results The four stable particles (neutrino, electron, neutron, proton) are the four stable states of a standing wave; masses from the speed of light alone: electron +0.7 %, nucleons about −3 % [result given hypotheses]. The Born rule, the randomness of a single outcome, the 2√2 limit in the Bell test, spin ½ and g = 2 [result]. The Lorentz transformation from the “speed budget” c² = v² + v_int², the Klein — Gordon and Schrödinger equations, Schwarzschild gravitational time dilation and the light deflection of 1.75″ [result]. Similarity of the small and the large with the step c⁴: the image of the neutron is the stellar mass of the Milky Way (5.5·10¹⁰ versus (6.1 ± 1.1)·10¹⁰ solar masses) [hypothesis, numerical agreement]. The large end is built by the same logic as the microworld: the construction yields the Hubble constant H₀ = 1/(5c²) ≈ 68.7 km/s/Mpc and the smallest acceleration of galaxies a₀ = 1/(10πc) [result given hypotheses]. The gravitational constant G ≈ c^(−6/5) (0.8 %); the mass of the Universe and the scale of dark energy are expressed through c [hypothesis]. The fine-structure constant has been found as the number 1/α ≈ 4·(c/2π)^(1/5) (0.22 %); its meaning is open [observation]. Limitations: the accuracy is percent-level, not parts per million; the standard and several constants remain open questions. The status of each statement is given in the text. Revision dated 2026-10-24:   The black hole. A black hole is understood as the construction of mass from the large end: particles build mass from the small end, the black hole from the large one. Perception has a limit of tempo: a process whose tempo is below our smallest does not change for us, so the centre is inaccessible, and for us it is space possessing mass and rotation. The horizon is the transition from space into mass; it grows with mass and is not related to the core. The black hole processes volumetric particles into a plane, and the tension of space, when the sizes of galaxies change, again gives birth to particle–antiparticle pairs: the cycle is closed. Only black holes that are analogues of elementary particles are considered. G and α. Both constants have received a geometric reading. Gravity is the work of space in a cross-section, charge is the same work over a closed surface; the surface of a sphere is four times its cross-section, hence the four. Charge is the work of one unpaired half-wave, that is, of one step of the microworld k: 1/α = 4k. G is gravity from the large end: the whole linear path up to the transition and the step linking it with the small end, G = 1/(c·c^(1/5)), without the four. The link of the two constants is G = 4α/((2π)^(1/5)·c). In neutral particles the same transition from flat to volume goes through rotation (support: the magnetic moment of the neutron).
